title: Arakhin 17
description: Chapter 3 closes with the aggada of rebuke and of leaders and their generations, and chapter 4, HaSeg Yad, opens: affordability follows the one who vows but a leper’s offering does not, a change in wealth before payment, and which of the leper’s offerings fixes his status.

a2.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַגָּדוֹל אוֹמֵר: אִלְמָלֵא בָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב בְּדִין, אֵין יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד מִפְּנֵי תּוֹכֵחָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְעַתָּה הִתְיַצְּבוּ וְאִשָּׁפְטָה אִתְּכֶם לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֵת כׇּל צִדְקוֹת ה׳ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אִתְּכֶם וְאֶת אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם״.

a3.he: ״זֶה דּוֹר דֹּרְשָׁיו מְבַקְשֵׁי פָנֶיךָ יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה״, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה וְרַבָּנַן, חַד אָמַר: דּוֹר לְפִי פַּרְנָס, וְחַד אָמַר: פַּרְנָס לְפִי דוֹרוֹ.

a4.he: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא? אִילֵּימָא לִמְעַלְּיוּתָא, דְּמָר סָבַר: אִי מְעַלֵּי דָּרָא מְעַלֵּי פַּרְנָס, וּמָר סָבַר: אִי מְעַלֵּי פַּרְנָס מְעַלֵּי דָּרָא — הָא אִיכָּא צִדְקִיָּה, דַּהֲוָה מְעַלֵּי וְדָרֵיהּ לָא הֲוָה מְעַלֵּי, וְהָא יְהוֹיָקִים, דְּלָא הֲוָה מְעַלֵּי וְדָרֵיהּ הֲוָה מְעַלֵּי!

a5.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״בְּרֵאשִׁית מַמְלְכוּת יְהוֹיָקִים מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה״?

a6.he: בִּיקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִיר אֶת הָעוֹלָם לְתוֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ בִּשְׁבִיל יְהוֹיָקִים, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּסְתַּכֵּל בְּדוֹרוֹ נִתְיַישְּׁבָה דַּעְתּוֹ. בִּיקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחְזִיר אֶת הָעוֹלָם לְתוֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ מִפְּנֵי דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל צִדְקִיָּהוּ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּסְתַּכֵּל בְּצִדְקִיָּהוּ נִתְיַישְּׁבָה דַּעְתּוֹ.

a9.he: מַתְנִי׳ הֶשֵּׂג יָד בַּנּוֹדֵר, וְהַשָּׁנִים בַּנִּידָּר, וְהָעֲרָכִין בַּנֶּעֱרָךְ, וְהָעֵרֶךְ בִּזְמַן הָעֵרֶךְ.

a10.he: הֶשֵּׂג יָד בַּנּוֹדֵר, כֵּיצַד? עָנִי שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הֶעָשִׁיר — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָנִי, וְעָשִׁיר שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הֶעָנִי — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָשִׁיר.

a11.he: אֲבָל בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת אֵינוֹ כֵּן, הֲרֵי שֶׁאָמַר: ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע זֶה עָלַי״, הָיָה מְצוֹרָע עָנִי — מֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָנִי, עָשִׁיר — מֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָשִׁיר.

a12.he: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר, אוֹמֵר אֲנִי: אַף בָּעֲרָכִין כֵּן, וְכִי מִפְּנֵי מָה עָנִי שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הֶעָשִׁיר נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָנִי, שֶׁאֵין הֶעָשִׁיר חַיָּיב כְּלוּם. אֲבָל עָשִׁיר שֶׁאָמַר: ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״, וְשָׁמַע עָנִי וְאָמַר: ״מַה שֶּׁאָמַר זֶה עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָשִׁיר.

a13.he: גְּמָ׳ הֶשֵּׂג יָד בַּמַּעֲרִיךְ הוּא! כְּדִכְתִיב: ״אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנּוֹדֵר יַעֲרִיכֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן״.

a14.he: הַשָּׁנִים בַּנִּידָּר? בַּנֶּעֱרָךְ הוּא! אַיְּידֵי דְּאָמַר ״הֶשֵּׂג יָד בַּנּוֹדֵר״, אָמַר נָמֵי ״הַשָּׁנִים בַּנִּידָּר״.

a15.he: הֶשֵּׂג יָד בַּנּוֹדֵר, כֵּיצַד? עָנִי שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הֶעָשִׁיר נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָנִי. מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר״ — בְּנוֹדֵר תְּלָה רַחֲמָנָא.

a16.he: אֲבָל בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת אֵינוֹ כֵּן, הֲרֵי שֶׁאָמַר: ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע זֶה עָלַי׳״, הָיָה מְצוֹרָע עָנִי מֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָנִי, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמַדִּירוֹ עָשִׁיר? וְאִם דַּל הוּא אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא דַּל הוּא.

a17.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כְּשֶׁהָיָה מַדִּירוֹ עָנִי, וְדִלְמָא עֲלֵיהּ דִּידֵיהּ חָס רַחֲמָנָא, אַמַּדִּירוֹ לָא, דְּהָכְתִיב: ״הוּא״.

a18.he: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: ״וְאֵין יָדוֹ מַשֶּׂגֶת״ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַנּוֹדֵר.

a19.he: אֲבָל מַדִּירוֹ עָשִׁיר, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּמַיְיתֵי בַּעֲשִׁירוּת?

a20.he: אִם כֵּן, מַאי ״אֲבָל בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת אֵינוֹ כֵּן״?

b1.he: חֲדָא אַמְּצוֹרָע עָנִי וּמַדִּירוֹ עָנִי, וַחֲדָא לְמַעוֹטֵי מְצוֹרָע עָשִׁיר וּמַדִּירוֹ עָנִי.

b2.he: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִיתְרַבּוֹ, אִיתְרַבּוֹ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b3.he: לְפִי שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּעֲרָכִין, עָנִי שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הֶעָשִׁיר נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָנִי, יָכוֹל אַף זֶה כֵּן, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִם דַּל הוּא״.

b4.he: וּלְרַבִּי, דְּאָמַר: ״אוֹמֵר אֲנִי אַף בַּעֲרָכִין כֵּן״ — אַלְמָא אָמַר: בָּתַר חִיּוּבָא דְּגַבְרָא אָזְלִינַן, וְהָא לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא לְמַעוֹטֵי הוּא, לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי?

b5.he: לְמַעוֹטֵי מְצוֹרָע עָנִי וּמַדִּירוֹ עָשִׁיר, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי: ״בָּתַר חִיּוּבָא דְּגַבְרָא אָזְלִינַן״, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b6.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה עָנִי וְהֶעֱשִׁיר, עָשִׁיר וְהֶעֱנִי — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָשִׁיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עָנִי וְהֶעֱשִׁיר וְחָזַר וְהֶעֱנִי — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָשִׁיר.

b7.he: אֲבָל בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת אֵינוֹ כֵּן, אֲפִילּוּ מֵת אָבִיו וְהִנִּיחַ לוֹ רִיבּוֹא, אוֹ סְפִינָתוֹ בַּיָּם וּבָאָה לוֹ בְּרִבּוֹאוֹת — אֵין לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ בָּהּ כְּלוּם.

b8.he: גְּמָ׳ עָנִי וְהֶעֱשִׁיר — ״אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר״. עָשִׁיר וְהֶעֱנִי — ״עַל פִּי אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג״.

b9.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ עָנִי וְהֶעֱשִׁיר וְחָזַר וְהֶעֱנִי — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ עָשִׁיר. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ״ — עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בְּמָכוּתוֹ מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ.

b10.he: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, וְאִם ״דַּל הוּא״, הָכִי נָמֵי עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בְּדַלּוּתוֹ מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ!

b11.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָתְנַן: מְצוֹרָע שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבְּנוֹתָיו עָנִי וְהֶעֱשִׁיר, עָשִׁיר וְהֶעֱנִי — הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר חַטָּאת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

b12.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר אָשָׁם, וְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר צִפֳּרִים!

b13.he: הָא אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: וּשְׁלׇשְׁתָּן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ, ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא תַשִּׂיג יָדוֹ בְּטׇהֳרָתוֹ״. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: דָּבָר הַמְכַפֵּר, מַאי נִיהוּ — חַטָּאת.

b14.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: דָּבָר הַמַּכְשִׁיר, וּמַאי נִיהוּ — אָשָׁם. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב סָבַר: הַגּוֹרֵם לוֹ טׇהֳרָה, וּמַאי נִיהוּ — צִיפֳּרִים.

b15.he: וְאֶלָּא ״הוּא״ לְמָה לִי? לְרַבִּי — כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ, וּלְרַבָּנַן — כִּדְאִית לְהוּ.

b16.he: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, ״וְהוּא עֵד״, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא כָּשֵׁר מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ!

b17.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָא תַּנְיָא: הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ לוֹ בְּעֵדוּת עַד שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה חֲתָנוֹ, וְנַעֲשָׂה חֲתָנוֹ, פִּקֵּחַ וְנִתְחָרֵשׁ, פָּתוּחַ וְנִסְתַּמֵּא, שָׁפוּי וְנִשְׁתַּטָּה — הֲרֵי זֶה פָּסוּל. אֲבָל הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ לוֹ עֵדוּת עַד שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה חֲתָנוֹ, וְנַעֲשָׂה חֲתָנוֹ,

messages.text: Continued from 16b: the Gemara asked why the minimum of suffering matters, and cited the school of Rabbi Yishmael: anyone who passes forty days without suffering has received his World. In the West, Eretz Yisrael, they say of him:
A calamity awaits him.

notes.he: למי שעברו עליו ארבעים יום בלא יסורין:
notes.en: A calamity awaits him: [this refers] to one over whom forty days have passed without suffering.

notes.he: ואם יארע לו אחת מאלו בתוך מ' יום נצול מאותו פורענות:
notes.en: A calamity awaits him: and if one of these [sufferings] befalls him within forty days, he is saved from that calamity.

messages.text: Were the Holy One, Blessed be He, to have entered into judgment with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, they would not have been able to stand before the rebuke. As it is stated: “Now therefore stand still, that I may plead with you before the Lord concerning all the righteous acts of the Lord, which He did to you and to your fathers” (I Samuel 12:7).
messages.lead: § The Gemara returns to the topic of rebuke. It is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:

verse.he: וְעַתָּה הִתְיַצְּבוּ וְאִשָּׁפְטָה אִתְּכֶם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֵת כׇּל־צִדְקוֹת יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה אִתְּכֶם וְאֶת־אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: Come, stand before GOD while I cite against you all the kindnesses that GOD has done to you and your ancestors.

notes.he: שהיה מוכיח להם מעשיהם:
notes.en: Before the rebuke: for He would reprove them for their deeds.

messages.text: This indicates that God acted towards the patriarchs with righteousness, i.e., mercy, not as they deserved according to the strict letter of the law.

notes.dh: צדקות ה' אשר עשה [אתכם ואת אבותיכם]
notes.he: מלמד שבצדקה עשה את אבותיכם ולא בדין:
notes.en: “The righteous acts of the Lord, which He did [to you and to your fathers]”: this teaches that He acted with your fathers in righteousness and not by strict judgment.

messages.text: § The verse states: “This is the generation of them that seek after Him, that seek Your face, Jacob. Selah” (Psalms 24:6). This verse teaches that the level of the generation and those who lead them, i.e., those who seek after Him, are the same.

verse.he: זֶה דּוֹר דֹּרְשָׁו מְבַקְשֵׁי פָנֶיךָ יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה׃
verse.en:
Such is the circle of those who turn to You,
Jacob, who seek Your presence. Selah.

notes.he: דמקיש דור לדורשיו:
notes.en: What is that which is written: “This is the generation of them that seek after Him [dorshav]”: it juxtaposes the generation [dor] to those who seek after Him [dorshav, i.e., its leaders].

notes.he: כלומר כדור כן דורשיו היינו מנהיגיו:
notes.en: “This is the generation of them that seek after Him”: that is to say, as the generation, so are those who seek after Him, namely, its leaders.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia and the Rabbis disagree about this.
The level of the generation follows the level of the leader,
The level of the leader follows the level of his generation.

With regard to what halakha, i.e., matter, is this stated? If we say for good, that one Sage holds that if the generation is good then their leader will be good, and one Sage holds that if the leader is good then his generation will be good,

notes.he: לענין חסידות:
notes.en: For good: with regard to piety.

messages.text: this cannot be correct, as there is the case of King Zedekiah, who was good, but his generation was not good. And conversely, there is the case of Jehoiakim who was not good, but his generation was good.
What is the meaning of that which is written: “In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, came this word from the Lord, saying” (Jeremiah 26:1),
messages.lead: The Gemara cites proof for these claims, as Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:

verse.he: בְּרֵאשִׁית מַמְלְכוּת יְהוֹיָקִים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה הָיָה הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה מֵאֵת יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר׃
verse.en: At the beginning of the reign of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah of Judah, this word came from GOD:

messages.text: and similarly with regard to Zedekiah the verse states: “And it came to pass the same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, that Hananiah, son of Azzur, the prophet, who was of Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the Lord, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying” (Jeremiah 28:1). Why did the prophet use the term “in the beginning” exclusively with regard to these two kings, as opposed to: During the first year of his reign, or a similar formulation?

verse.he: וַיְהִי ׀ בַּשָּׁנָה הַהִיא בְּרֵאשִׁית מַמְלֶכֶת צִדְקִיָּה מֶלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה (בשנת) [בַּשָּׁנָה] הָרְבִעִית בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁי אָמַר אֵלַי חֲנַנְיָה בֶן־עַזּוּר הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר מִגִּבְעוֹן בְּבֵית יְהֹוָה לְעֵינֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים וְכׇל־הָעָם לֵאמֹר׃
verse.en: That year, early in the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, in the fifth month of the fourth year, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, who was from Gibeon, spoke to me in the House of GOD, in the presence of the priests and all the people. He said:

notes.he: מאי שנא דכתיב ביהויקים וצדקיהו בראשית לפי שביקש הקב"ה להפוך מעשה בראשית בימיהם:
notes.en: What is different that “in the beginning [bereshit]” is written with regard to Jehoiakim and Zedekiah? Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to overturn the act of Creation [ma’aseh bereshit] in their days.

messages.text: This term teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to revert the world to chaos and void, as it was in the beginning before Creation (Genesis 1:1–2), on account of Jehoiakim, who did evil in the eyes of God. Once He observed the people of his generation, His mind was settled.
Likewise, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to revert the world to chaos and void, on account of the generation of Zedekiah, but once He observed Zedekiah, His mind was settled.
This shows that the leader and his generation are not necessarily on the same level in terms of righteousness.
Rather, we are speaking in terms of harshness and gentleness.

notes.he: כעס:
notes.en: Harshness [tukfa]: anger.

notes.he: נוח לרצות:
notes.en: Gentleness [niḥuta]: easy to appease.

messages.text: One Sage holds that if the leader is harsh, then the generation will be harsh. If the leader is gentle and kind, the generation will be the same. The other Sage holds that if the people of a certain generation are harsh, they will have a harsh leader; if the generation is gentle and kind, the leader will be similar.

notes.he: כלומר שאם המנהיג קפדן כך כל הקהל וכן נמי אם הוא עניו אף כולן כן:
notes.en: With regard to harshness and gentleness: that is to say, if the leader is exacting, so is the whole community; and likewise, if he is humble, they are all so as well.

notes.he: הדרן עלך יש בערכין
notes.en: We will return to you, Yesh BaArakhin. [Rabbeinu Gershom marks the end of the chapter here.]

messages.text: הדרן עלך יש בערכין · Hadran alakh Yesh BaArakhin: we will return to you, chapter 3, “There Are [Halakhot] with Regard to Valuations [That Are Lenient and Stringent].”

Chapter 4 · השג יד · HaSeg Yad: the valuation is set by the means of the one who vows, the sum by the age and sex of the one valuated and by the time of the vow, and how the offerings of a leper differ.
Mishna

Affordability, which is written in the Torah: “According to the means of him who vowed shall the priest valuate him” (Leviticus 27:8), is determined in accordance with the means of the one taking the vow, and the sum fixed by the Torah based on the years of age is in accordance with the age of the subject of the vow.

verse.he: וְאִם־מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן עַל־פִּי אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר יַעֲרִיכֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן׃ {ס}
verse.en: But if someone cannot afford the equivalent, they shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall make an assessment; the priest shall make the assessment according to what the vower can afford.

notes.he: תורת דין השג יד שהעני נידון בערכין לפי השג ידו כדכתיב ואם מך הוא מערכך בתר נודר אזלינן ולא בתר נידר כדמפרש לקמן:
notes.en: Mishna. Affordability in accordance with the one taking the vow: the law of affordability, that a poor person is judged in valuations according to his means, as it is written: “But if he is too poor for your valuation” (Leviticus 27:8). We follow the one taking the vow and not the subject of the vow, as is explained below.

notes.he: כדמפרש לקמן ילד שהעריך זקן נותן ערך זקן דלא אזלינן בתר שנים דידיה דנודר דהא לא אמר ערכי עלי אלא ערך פלוני עלי וערך זקן מבן ששים ומעלה פחות מערך ילד:
notes.en: And the years in accordance with the subject of the vow: as is explained below, a young person who valuated an elderly person gives the valuation of an elderly person. For we do not follow the years of the one taking the vow himself, since he did not say: My valuation is upon me, but rather: The valuation of so-and-so is upon me. And the valuation of an elderly person, from sixty years and up, is less than the valuation of a young person.

notes.dh: מתני' השג יד בנודר והשנים בנידר והערכין בנערך
notes.he: תימה אמאי לא ערבינהו בהדי הדדי וליתני השנים והערכין בנערך ועוד תימ' אמאי לא תני זכר נותן ערך נקבה ולא איצטריך לקמן לומר הערכי' בנערך כו':
notes.en: Mishna. Affordability in accordance with the one taking the vow, and the years in accordance with the subject of the vow, and the valuations in accordance with the one valuated: This is puzzling: why did he not combine them together and teach: The years and the valuations are in accordance with the one valuated? And it is further puzzling: why did he not teach: A male gives the valuation of a female [i.e., state the case directly], and then it would not have been necessary below to say: The valuations in accordance with the one valuated, etc.?

notes.he: [השג יד דכתיב על פי אשר תשיג יד הנודר יעריכנו בתר השג יד דמעריך אזלינן דהיינו נודר כדמפרש בגמרא ולא בתר נערך כדמפרש כיצד עני שהעריך כו':
notes.en: Affordability in accordance with the one taking the vow: affordability, as it is written: “According to the means of him who vowed shall he valuate him”: we follow the means of the one who valuates, that is, the one taking the vow, as is explained in the Gemara, and not the one valuated, as he explains: How so? A poor person who valuated, etc.

notes.he: היינו כערך מה שכתוב [בתורה] אם מבן חדש שנים אם מבן עשרים בתר שנים דנערך אזלינן ולא בתר מעריך ומפרש כיצד כו' אכל חד וחד]:
notes.en: And the years in accordance with the subject of the vow: that is, as the valuation written [in the Torah], whether from a month old or from twenty years: we follow the years of the one valuated and not of the one who valuates. And he explains: How so, etc., for each one.

messages.text: And the distinction based on sex that is written in the halakhot of valuations is stated with regard to the one valuated, and the different valuation based on the age of the one valuated is determined at the time one takes the vow of valuation.

notes.he: קצב הערך דזכר ונקבה בתר נערך אזיל ולא בתר מעריך כדמפרש לקמן איש שהעריך אשה דאמר ערך פלונית עלי נותן ערך הנערך:
notes.en: And the valuations in accordance with the one valuated: the fixed sum of the valuation for a male and a female follows the one valuated and not the one who valuates, as is explained below: a man who valuated a woman, saying: The valuation of so-and-so [a woman] is upon me, gives the valuation of the one valuated.

notes.he: כדמפרש לקמן שאם העריך עצמו פחות מבן עשרים דהוי ערך קטן וקודם נתינתו נעשה בן עשרים אינו נותן אלא כשעה שהעריך תחילה:
notes.en: At the time of the valuation: as is explained below, that if he valuated himself when he was less than twenty years old, which is the valuation of a minor, and before he gave it he became twenty, he gives only according to the time when he first valuated.

messages.text: Affordability is in accordance with the means of the one taking the vow; how so? A destitute person who valuated a wealthy person gives the valuation in accordance with the means of a destitute person, as determined by the priest. And a wealthy person who valuated a destitute person gives the valuation in accordance with the means of a wealthy person, the sum of which is fixed in the Torah.

notes.dh: כיצד עני שהעריך את העשיר כו'
notes.he: (פי' רש"י) לעיל (ערכין דף ז:) פרק אין נערכין פחות כו':
notes.en: How so? A poor person who valuated a wealthy person, etc.: [this was explained] above (Arakhin 7b), in the chapter Ein Ne’erakhin Paḥot, etc. [The printed text has the words “Rashi explained” in parentheses here.]

messages.text: But with regard to offerings that is not so, as one who took a vow and said: It is incumbent upon me to provide the offering of this leper, to a leper who requires it for his purification;

notes.he: דלא אזלינן בתר השג יד דמדיר אלא [דנידר] כדמפרש הרי שאמר קרבנות של מצורע זה עלי יש שמביא תחתיו:
notes.en: But with regard to offerings [that is not so]: for we do not follow the means of the one who vows for him but [of the subject of the vow], as he explains: If one said: The offerings of this leper are upon me. [A note in the printed text suggests reading: If this one in whose place he brings was a poor leper, etc.]

messages.text: if the one undergoing purification was a destitute leper, the one who took the vow brings the offering of a destitute leper, which is one male sheep, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, and two doves or two pigeons (see Leviticus 14:21–22). If the one undergoing purification was a wealthy leper, the one who took the vow brings the offering of a wealthy leper, which is two male sheep, a ewe, and three-tenths of a ephah of fine flour (see Leviticus 14:10).

notes.he: היה מצורע עני [מביא קרבן עני] כו':
notes.en: If it was a poor leper, [he brings a poor person’s offering], etc.

messages.text: I say: Even with regard to valuations it is so.

notes.he: אילו מתרמי בערכין דומיא דקרבנות הוי כקרבנות דהא דאמרת דערכין אינן כקרבנות משום דלא דמו אהדדי דמפני מה עני שהעריך עשיר נותן ערך עני לפי השג ידו משום דאין העשיר חייב כלום ולא דמי למצורע וזה שאמר על העשיר לא נתכוון אלא לפי מדת שנותיו של העשיר שפחותין או יתירין על שנותיו שלו הלכך נידון בהשג יד דהא לא פירש כלום אלא ערך מדת [שנותיו של] העשיר קיבל עליו ודין ערך נידון בהשג יד:
notes.en: I say: even with regard to valuations it is so: if a case should occur with valuations similar to the offerings, it would be like the offerings. As for what you said, that valuations are not like offerings, that is because the cases are not similar to one another. For why does a poor person who valuated a wealthy person give the valuation of a poor person, according to his means? Because the wealthy person is not obligated anything, and it is not similar to the leper [who is himself obligated in his offering]. And this one who spoke of the wealthy person intended only the measure of the wealthy person’s years, which are fewer or more than his own years. Therefore he is judged by affordability, for he specified nothing except that he took upon himself the valuation of the measure [of the years] of the wealthy person, and the law of a valuation is that it is judged by affordability.

notes.dh: מתני' רבי אומר אומר אני אף בערכין כן
notes.he: כמו בקרבנות דאזלינן בתר נידר:
notes.en: Mishna. Rabbi says: I say: even with regard to valuations it is so: as with offerings, where we follow the subject of the vow.

messages.text: For what reason does a destitute person who valuated a wealthy person give the valuation in accordance with the means of a destitute person? It is due to the fact that the wealthy person is not obligated to pay anything, as the debt was generated by the destitute person who vowed to donate the valuation of a wealthy individual.

notes.he: כלומר [אם כן] מפני מה קתני רישא דמתני' עני שהעריך את העשיר נותן ערך עני דאזלינן בתר השג יד דנודר לפי שאין העשיר הנערך חייב כלום אבל עשיר שאמר [ערכי עלי שחייב בערכו ושמע עני] כו' אזלינן בתר השג יד דנידר דומיא דקרבנות:
notes.en: For why, etc.: that is to say, [if so,] why does the first clause of the mishna teach: A poor person who valuated a wealthy person gives the valuation of a poor person, following the means of the one taking the vow? Because the wealthy person who is valuated is not obligated anything. But a wealthy person who said: [My valuation is upon me, who is obligated in his valuation, and a poor person heard], etc., we follow the means of the subject of the vow, similar to offerings.

messages.text: But in a case similar to that of the offerings of a leper, in the case of a wealthy person who said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and a destitute person heard him and said: It is incumbent upon me to donate that which he said, the destitute person gives the valuation of a wealthy person.

notes.he: דהוי חייב ערך שלם דומיא דמצורע עשיר ושמע עני וכו':
notes.en: But a wealthy person who said: My valuation is upon me: who is obligated in a full valuation, similar to a wealthy leper; and a poor person heard, etc.

messages.text: Gemara

The halakha of affordability is written in the Torah with regard to the case of one who valuates, i.e., one who says he will give the Temple treasury the set sum assigned to a particular individual’s age and sex. Why, then, is the mishna referring to affordability in the context of one pledging another’s worth by taking a vow, in which the obligation is calculated individually rather than by predetermined assigned values?
messages.quote: Affordability is determined in accordance with the means of the one taking the vow

notes.dh: גמ' וקפריך השג יד במעריך הוא
notes.he: ולא בנודר שהאומר דמי עלי אין נידון בהשג יד אלא הכל יתן כשיוכל דאמרינן בפרק האומר משקלי עלי (לקמן ערכין כ.) חומר בנדרים מבערכין שהנדרים אין נידונים בהשג יד:
notes.en: Gemara. And he objects: Affordability applies to one who valuates: and not to one who vows. For one who says: My worth is upon me, is not judged by affordability; rather, he gives all of it when he is able, as we say in the chapter HaOmer Mishkali Alai (below, Arakhin 20a): Vows are more stringent than valuations, in that vows are not judged by affordability.

notes.he: פי' במעריך דוקא לא בנודר כדקאמרי' לקמן בהאומר משקלי (ערכין דף כ.) חומר בנדרים מבערכין שהנדרים חלים על הבהמה ועוף ואין נידונין בהשג יד מה שאין כן בערכין (והוא למעוטי מצורע עשיר):
notes.en: Affordability in accordance with the one taking the vow? It applies to one who valuates: that is, specifically to one who valuates and not to one who vows, as we say below in the chapter HaOmer Mishkali (Arakhin 20a): Vows are more stringent than valuations, in that vows take effect on an animal and a bird, and they are not judged by affordability, which is not so with valuations. [The printed text adds in parentheses: And it comes to exclude a wealthy leper.]

notes.he: [וקא בעי אמאי תני תנא השג יד בנודר הא בנדרים לא אזלינן בתר השג יד אלא בערכין במעריך ומתרץ דהאי נודר דקתני היינו מעריך ואמאי תני נודר בתר לישנא דקרא אזיל דכתיב על פי אשר תשיג יד הנודר יעריכנו קא קרי למעריך נודר והשנים בנידר]:
notes.en: And he asks: Why does the tanna teach affordability in accordance with the one taking the vow? With vows we do not follow affordability, only with valuations, with the one who valuates. And he answers that this “one taking the vow” that he teaches is the one who valuates. And why does he teach “one taking the vow”? He follows the language of the verse, as it is written: “According to the means of him who vowed shall he valuate him.” [A note in the printed text gives the end as:] And since he calls the one who valuates “one who vows,” he also says: The years in accordance with the subject of the vow.

messages.text: The mishna employs the language of the verse, which uses the word “vow,” as it is written: “According to the means of him who vowed shall the priest valuate him” (Leviticus 27:8).

notes.dh: ומשני כדכתיב על פי אשר תשיג וגו'
notes.he: כלומר האי דקרי למעריך הכא נודר דלישנא דקרא נקט:
notes.en: And he answers: As it is written: “According to the means,” etc.: that is to say, the reason he calls the one who valuates “one who vows” here is that he adopted the wording of the verse.

messages.text: Similarly, is the mishna’s wording accurate when it states that the sum of the obligation based on the years of age is in accordance with the age of the subject of the vow? The mishna should state that the sum based on years is determined in accordance with the age of the subject of the valuation, not the vow.
messages.quote: the years of age is in accordance with the age of the subject of the vow

notes.he: דהאומר דמי פלוני עלי אין נידון לפי מדת שנים אלא כפי שאותו פלוני נמכר בשוק:
notes.en: The years in accordance with the one valuated and not the subject of the vow: for one who says: The worth of so-and-so is upon me, is not judged according to the measure of years, but according to what that so-and-so would sell for in the market.

messages.text: Although it is discussing valuations, since the mishna uses the term vow when it says: Affordability is determined in accordance with the means of the one taking the vow, the mishna also deploys the same term when it says: The sum of the obligation based on the years of age is in accordance with the age of the subject of the vow.

The mishna further teaches: Affordability is in accordance with the one taking the vow; how so? A destitute person who valuated a wealthy person gives the valuation in accordance with the means of the destitute person.
messages.quote: A destitute person who valuated a wealthy person gives the valuation

notes.dh: השג יד בנודר כיצד עני שהעריך את העשיר נותן ערך עני
notes.he: מפי הר"ר מנחם מיאונ"י כגון עשיר שאמר ערכי עלי ושמע עני ואמר זה עלי נותן ערך עני אבל בקרבנות אינו כן הרי שאמר קרבן של מצורע זה עלי כו' אהא פליג רבי ואומר עשיר שאמר ערכי עלי ושמע עני ואומר מה שאמר זה עלי נותן ערך עשיר כמו בקרבנות וכן משמע פי' דמתני':
notes.en: Affordability in accordance with the one taking the vow; how so? A poor person who valuated a wealthy person gives the valuation of a poor person: from the mouth of Rabbi Menaḥem of Joigny: for example, a wealthy person who said: My valuation is upon me, and a poor person heard and said: This is upon me, gives the valuation of a poor person. But with offerings it is not so: if one said: The offering of this leper is upon me, etc. On this Rabbi disagrees and says: A wealthy person who said: My valuation is upon me, and a poor person heard and said: What this one said is upon me, gives the valuation of a wealthy person, as with offerings. And so the explanation of the mishna implies.

messages.text: What is the reason? As the verse states: “According to the means of him who vowed,” which teaches that the Merciful One renders the matter dependent on the one who vows, not upon the subject of the vow.

notes.he: בנודר תלה רחמנא השג יד דאי עני הוא נותן שקל ופטור אפילו יעשיר אח"כ ואם לא נתן שקל בעניותו אם יעשיר יתן ערך שלם:
notes.en: The Merciful One made affordability depend on the one who vows: for if he is poor, he gives a sela and is exempt, even if he becomes wealthy afterward; and if he did not give the sela in his poverty, if he becomes wealthy he gives the full valuation.

messages.text: But with regard to offerings that is not so, as in the case of one who vowed and said: It is incumbent upon me to provide the offering of this leper, if the one undergoing purification was a destitute leper, the one who vowed brings the offering of a destitute leper.
messages.quote: But with regard to offerings that is not so

notes.he: אלא תלינן השג יד בנידר:
notes.en: But with regard to offerings that is not so: rather, we make the affordability depend on the subject of the vow.

messages.text: And is this the halakha even though it was a wealthy person who takes the vow to provide the offerings for him?

notes.he: בתמיה. מדירו היינו זה שאמר קרבן מצורע עלי:
notes.en: And even though the one who vows for him is wealthy?: this is a question [i.e., can that be so?]. “The one who vows for him [madiro]” is the one who said: The offering of the leper is upon me.

notes.he: יביא קרבן עני כשהנידר עני:
notes.en: And even though the one who vows for him is wealthy?: he brings a poor person’s offering when the subject of the vow is poor?

messages.text: But the Merciful One states: “And if he is poor, and his means do not suffice, then he shall take one sheep” (Leviticus 14:21). This indicates that the specified offering is only for the poor, and in this instance the one taking the vow is not poor.

verse.he: וְאִם־דַּל הוּא וְאֵין יָדוֹ מַשֶּׂגֶת וְלָקַח כֶּבֶשׂ אֶחָד אָשָׁם לִתְנוּפָה לְכַפֵּר עָלָיו וְעִשָּׂרוֹן סֹלֶת אֶחָד בָּלוּל בַּשֶּׁמֶן לְמִנְחָה וְלֹג שָׁמֶן׃
verse.en: If, however, the person is poor and without sufficient means, they shall take one male lamb for a reparation offering, to be elevated in expiation, one-tenth of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in for a grain offering, and a log of oil;

notes.he: המביא קרבן אמר רחמנא יביא קרבן עני והאי מדירו דחייב להביא קרבן עשיר הוא ואמאי מביא קרבן עני:
notes.en: But “if he is poor”: of the one bringing the offering the Merciful One said that he brings a poor person’s offering; and this one who vows for him is obligated to bring a wealthy person’s offering. So why does he bring a poor person’s offering?

messages.text: The mishna is referring specifically to a case where it was a poor person who was taking the vow to provide the offerings for the leper.

notes.he: הלכך מביא קרבן עני:
notes.en: When the one who vows for him was [also] poor: therefore he brings a poor person’s offering.

messages.text: But what is the basis for this ruling? Perhaps the Merciful One had compassion on him, i.e., the leper, and not on the one taking the vow to provide the offerings for him. As isn’t it written: “And if he is poor”? If so, the leniency that a destitute leper brings less expensive offerings should apply only to an actual leper, and not to one who vows to bring the leper’s offerings, even if he too is poor.

notes.he: דמצורע חס רחמנא אדלות אבל אמדירו לא ואע"ג דהוי עני:
notes.en: Perhaps on him: on the leper the Merciful One had compassion in his poverty, but not on the one who vows for him, even though he is poor.

notes.he: על מצורע עצמו כשהוא דל חס רחמנא עליה דלייתי בדלות אבל מדירו שאמר קרבנותיו עלי אף על גב דעני הוא לא חס רחמנא עליה אלא לייתי קרבן עשיר דהא כתיב הוא כלומר דהוא מצורע לייתי בדלות אבל לא מדירו:
notes.en: [And why?] Perhaps on him: on the leper himself, when he is poor, the Merciful One had compassion, that he may bring in poverty; but on the one who vows for him, who said: His offerings are upon me, even though he is poor, the Merciful One did not have compassion, and he must bring a wealthy person’s offering. For it is written “he,” that is to say, he, the leper, brings in poverty, but not the one who vows for him.

messages.text: The next clause in the verse: “And his means do not suffice,” serves to include the one taking the vow to provide the offering, i.e., if he too is poor he provides the offering mandated for a destitute leper.

notes.dh: (אמר רחמנא) [אמר רב אדא הדר כתיב] ואין ידו משגת
notes.he: דלא צריך למכתב דהא כתיב ואם דל הוא אלא ואין ידו משגת לרבות את (הנודר) [המדיר] דכשהוא עני דמייתי נמי קרבן עני:
notes.en: [Rav Adda said: It is further written:] “And his means do not suffice”: this did not need to be written, since it is written: “And if he is poor.” Rather, “and his means do not suffice” comes to include the one who vows for him, that when he is poor he too brings a poor person’s offering.

messages.text: But according to this answer, when a wealthy person takes the vow to provide the offering for him, so too, the halakha is that he brings the offering of the leper brought in a situation of wealth.
messages.quote: where it was a poor person who was taking the vow

notes.dh: אבל מדירו עשיר מאי הכי נמי דמייתי בעשירות א"ה מאי אבל בקרבנות אינו כן
notes.he: והלא בקרבנות כמו כן הדין שאם אמר עשיר קרבנות של מצורע עני זה עלי מביא קרבן עשיר וא"כ מאי חילוק יש בקרבנות לערכין ומשני אחדא פי' אמצורע עשיר ומדירו עני דאילו גבי מצורע אם אמר עני קרבן של מצורע עשיר זה עלי נותן ערך עשיר דלא אזלינן בתר הנודר ובערכין אזלינן בתר הנודר דאילו אמר עשיר ערכי עלי ושמע עני [ואמר] מה שאמר זה עלי נותן ערך עני דאזלינן בתר הנודר ומש"ה איצטריך הוא למעוטי גביה דלא אזלינן בתר נודר כמו בערכין ולרבי דאמר ערכין וקרבן שוין בדין זה אם כן לא איצטריך הוא למעוטי מצורע עשיר שמדירו עני דנותן ערך עשיר שהרי גבי ערכין כן הדין אלא איצטריך הוא למעוטי מצורע עני ומדירו עשיר דס"ד הואיל ורבי בתר חיובא דגברא אזיל ה"נ ניזיל בתר חיובא דגברא ונייתי קרבן עני קמ"ל דלא אבל לרבנן לא איצטריך הוא למעוטי מצורע עני ומדירו עשיר דהואיל דבערכין אזלינן בתר נודר פשיטא דבמצורע נמי אזלינן בתר נודר ולא איצטריך הוא להכי כדפי' וכן פירש רש"י וכי דייקינן בסוגיא דשמעתין כן הוא אבל צריך עיון לרבי דמדמה אמר העשיר ערכי עלי לקרבנות דמצורע עשיר דעני הנודר בעי לאיתויי קרבן עשיר והיינו דוקא כשאמר העני הרי עלי קרבנות מצורע זה לפוטרו ואם אמר כן בערכין מאי טעמא דרבנן כיון שאמר הרי מה שאמר זה עלי לפוטרו אם כן נדר בהדיא חמשים סלעים ואיך נפטר בערך עני:
notes.en: But if the one who vows for him is wealthy, so too he brings in wealth? If so, what is: But with regard to offerings it is not so?: For with offerings the law is the same: if a wealthy person said: The offerings of this poor leper are upon me, he brings a wealthy person’s offering. So what difference is there between offerings and valuations? And he answers: One [clause] is about a wealthy leper whose vower is poor. For with a leper, if a poor person said: The offering of this wealthy leper is upon me, he gives [that] of a wealthy person, since we do not follow the one who vows; whereas with valuations we follow the one who vows, for if a wealthy person said: My valuation is upon me, and a poor person heard [and said]: What this one said is upon me, he gives the valuation of a poor person, since we follow the one who vows. Therefore “he” is needed to exclude [the leper], that there we do not follow the one who vows as with valuations. But according to Rabbi, who says that valuations and the offering are equal in this law, “he” is not needed to exclude a wealthy leper whose vower is poor, who gives [the offering] of a wealthy person, since with valuations the law is the same. Rather, “he” is needed to exclude a poor leper whose vower is wealthy: it might enter your mind that since Rabbi follows the obligation of the person, here too we should follow the obligation of the person and bring a poor person’s offering; it teaches us that it is not so. But according to the Rabbis, “he” is not needed to exclude a poor leper whose vower is wealthy: since with valuations we follow the one who vows, it is obvious that with the leper too we follow the one who vows, and “he” is not needed for this, as I explained. And so Rashi explained, and when we analyze the discussion here, so it is. But Rabbi’s view requires study: he compares a wealthy person who said: My valuation is upon me, to the offerings of a wealthy leper, where a poor person who vows must bring a wealthy person’s offering; and that is specifically when the poor person said: The offerings of this leper are upon me, to exempt him. And if he said so with valuations, what is the reason of the Rabbis? Since he said: What this one said is upon me, to exempt him, he has then explicitly vowed fifty sela, so how is he exempted with a poor person’s valuation?

notes.he: אבל מדירו עשיר [מאי] הכי נמי [דמייתי בעשירות] אע"ג (דהמודר) [דמצורע] הוי עני אלמא דבתר מדיר אזלינן מאי אבל בקרבנות אינו כן כלומר דאזיל בתר נידר הא קא חזינן מדוקיא דאזיל [נמי] בתר מדיר כמו בערכין:
notes.en: But if the one who vows for him is wealthy, [what?] So too [he brings in wealth], even though the leper is poor? Evidently we follow the one who vows for him. What then is: But with regard to offerings that is not so, that is to say, that we follow the subject of the vow? For we see from the precise reading that we [also] follow the one who vows for him, as with valuations.

messages.text: If so, what is the meaning of the mishna’s statement that valuations are determined based on the means of the one making the commitment, but with regard to offerings, that is not so?

notes.he: הא בקרבנות נמי אזלת בתר נודר:
notes.en: What is: But with regard to offerings that is not so?: But with offerings too you follow the one taking the vow!

messages.text: This clause seems to indicate that unlike the previous ruling, where a wealthy person who valuated a destitute individual gives the valuation in accordance with the means of a wealthy person, here it all depends on the means of the one undergoing purification. Therefore, in this case a wealthy person brings the offerings of one who is destitute, contrary to the statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak.

The mishna states two different principles with regard to one who vows to provide the offering of a leper on behalf of another. One principle applies to a destitute leper for whom another destitute person takes a vow to provide his offering. In that case, he provides the offering of the destitute.

notes.dh: ומשני חדא אמצורע עני ומדירו עני וחדא למעוטי מצורע עשיר ומדירו עני
notes.he: כלומר ודאי חדא מהנך מילי דמתני' דהיינו הך דקתני אם היה מצורע עני מביא קרבן עני ודאי במדירו עני קמיירי וכדאוקימנא ומאידך מילתא נפקא לן דבקרבנות אינו כן דקתני אם היה מצורע עשיר מביא קרבן עשיר ואע"ג דמדירו עני והיינו למעוטי מדיר מדין ערכין דלא אזלינן בתר נודר:
notes.en: And he answers: One is about a poor leper whose vower is poor, and one is to exclude a wealthy leper whose vower is poor: that is to say, certainly one of these statements of the mishna, namely the one that teaches: If it was a poor leper he brings a poor person’s offering, certainly speaks where his vower is poor, as we established. And from the other statement we derive that with offerings it is not so, which teaches: If it was a wealthy leper he brings a wealthy person’s offering, even though his vower is poor; and this is to exclude the vower from the law of valuations, for [here] we do not follow the one who vows.

messages.text: And the one other principle, i.e., the statement that the halakha is different in the case of offerings, serves to exclude the case of a wealthy leper for whom a destitute person takes a vow to provide his offering. In that situation, although the one who took the vow is destitute, he must provide the offering of a wealthy person.

notes.he: לעולם בקרבנות אזלינן בתר נידר דהיינו מצורע וחדא אמצורע עני וכו' דתרי מעוטי כתיבי בקרא חדא ואין ידו משגת אתי אמצורע עני ומדירו עני דמייתי מדירו בדלות כדאמרינן ואין ידו משגת לרבות את הנודר ואכתי מהכא לא ילפינן אבל בקרבנות אינו כן דכיון דמדיר נמי עני הוא אף על גב דמייתי בדלות לא ידעינן אי אזלינן בתר נידר או בתר מדיר אלא מהכא ילפינן דבקרבנו' אינו כן [דחדא] דכתיב ואם דל הוא הוא המצורע מייתי בדלות למעוטי מצורע עשיר ומדירו עני דהמדיר לא מייתי בדלות אלא [ידעינן אי אזיל בתר נידר או בתר מדיר] בעשירות והיינו אבל בקרבנות אינו כן אלא תלינן השג יד בנידר במצורע. דסד"א הואיל ואיתרבי מדיר לקרבן מצורע עני מואין ידו משגת [לאייתויי בדלות הנודר] איתרבי נמי השתא ואע"ג דהמצורע הוא עשיר הואיל והמדיר הוי עני דלייתי [נמי] בדלות קמ"ל הוא דבדלות דמצורע תלינן כדתניא לפי שמצינו כו':
notes.en: Actually, with offerings we follow the subject of the vow, that is, the leper; and one is about a poor leper, etc. For two exclusions are written in the verse. One, “and his means do not suffice,” comes for a poor leper whose vower is poor, that the vower brings in poverty, as we said: “and his means do not suffice” includes the one who vows. But from here we still do not learn “but with regard to offerings that is not so”; for since the vower too is poor, even though he brings in poverty, we do not know whether we follow the subject of the vow or the vower. Rather, from here we learn that with offerings it is not so: one, for it is written “and if he is poor,” he, the leper, brings in poverty, to exclude a wealthy leper whose vower is poor, that the vower does not bring in poverty but in wealth; [and from this we know that we follow the subject of the vow and not the vower]. And this is: But with regard to offerings that is not so; rather, we make the affordability depend on the subject of the vow, the leper. For it might enter your mind to say: since the vower was included for the offering of a poor leper from “and his means do not suffice” [to bring in poverty], he is now also included even though the leper is wealthy, since the vower is poor, that he [too] brings in poverty. It teaches us “he”: that we depend on the poverty of the leper, as it is taught: Since we find, etc. [The printed text has editorial corrections in this note; we follow them.]

messages.text: It might enter your mind to say: Since the destitute were included in the verse: “And his means do not suffice,” with regard to the leniency which allows them to bring the offering of the destitute when taking vows to provide for destitute lepers, they should likewise be included in this leniency when providing for all lepers, even wealthy ones. Consequently, the tanna teaches us that this leniency does not apply when the lepers are wealthy.

notes.he: כלומר ואיצטריך לאשמועינן אבל בקרבנות אינו כן לאשמועינן דהיכא דמצורע עשיר ומדירו עני מביא קרבן עשיר דסד"א הואיל ואיתרבי נודר מואין ידו משגת דחס רחמנא עליה כי הוי איהו עני ומצורע עני אתרבי נמי אפילו היכא דמצורע עשיר הואיל והוא עני קמ"ל. לי נראה ועיקר דה"ג אם כן מאי אבל בקרבנות אינו כן אחדא אמצורע עשיר ומדירו עני סד"א כו' ואני שמעתיה כמות שהיא כתובה בספרים ופירושה כמו שפירשתיה ואין כן שיטת הש"ס:
notes.en: It might enter your mind to say, etc.: that is to say, and it was necessary to teach us “but with regard to offerings that is not so,” to teach us that where the leper is wealthy and his vower poor, he brings a wealthy person’s offering. For it might enter your mind to say: since the one who vows was included from “and his means do not suffice,” in that the Merciful One had compassion on him when he is poor and the leper is poor, he is also included even where the leper is wealthy, since he is poor; it teaches us [otherwise]. To me it seems, and this is the main reading, that the text reads: If so, what is: But with regard to offerings that is not so? It is about one case, about a wealthy leper whose vower is poor; it might enter your mind, etc. But I learned it as it is written in the books, and its explanation is as I have explained it, though that is not the [natural] flow of the Talmud.

messages.text: Since we find with regard to valuations that a destitute person who valuated a wealthy person gives the valuation in accordance with the means of a destitute person, one might have thought that in this case, where one takes a vow to provide the offering of a wealthy leper, the halakha is also so.
messages.lead: Similarly, it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: עני שאמר קרבן מצורע עשיר זה עלי:
notes.en: Might this too be so: a poor person who said: The offering of this wealthy leper is upon me.

notes.he: תימה בלאו הני טעמא דמצינו בערכין הל"ל גבי מצורע דעני שאמר קרבן מצורע עלי נותן ערך עני מריבויא דאין ידו משגת לרבות את הנודר כדדריש לעיל ויש לומר דמכל מקום אי לא אשכחן בערכין כה"ג לא הוה לן למידרש עני שהעריך את העשיר מריבויא דקרא אם אין ידו משגת:
notes.en: Since we find with regard to valuations: This is puzzling: even without this reason of “we find with regard to valuations,” it should have said with regard to a leper that a poor person who said: The offering of the leper is upon me, gives [the offering] of a poor person, from the inclusion of “and his means do not suffice,” to include the one who vows, as was expounded above. And one can say: In any case, had we not found such a case with valuations, we would not have expounded [the case of] a poor person who valuated a wealthy person from the inclusion of the verse “and his means do not suffice.”

notes.he: מי שאמר קרבנו של מצורע עשיר זה עלי והוא עני שיבא בדלות ת"ל אם דל הוא למעוטי מדיר:
notes.en: Might this too be so: one who said: The offering of this wealthy leper is upon me, and he is poor, that he should bring in poverty; the verse states: “If he is poor,” to exclude the vower.

messages.text: Consequently, the verse states: “And if he is poor,” from which it is derived that the offering of the destitute leper is brought only when the leper himself is destitute.

notes.he: חס רחמנא עליה ולא על מדירו:
notes.en: “If he is poor”: the Merciful One had compassion on him, and not on the one who vows for him.

messages.text: But according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, this is difficult. As he says in the mishna: I say even with regard to valuations it is so, i.e., that if a wealthy person said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and a destitute person heard him and said: It is incumbent upon me to donate that which he said, then the destitute person gives the valuation of a wealthy person.
messages.quote: I say: Even with regard to valuations it is so

notes.he: דאי הוי עשיר מחוייב ערך ואמר עני מה שאמר זה עלי נותן ערך עשיר אלמא בתר חיובא דגברא דנערך אזלינן היכא דהוא חייב כלום דומיא דמצורע והא דמצורע עשיר ומדירו עני לא צריכא למעוטי דמערכין נפקא לן דמייתי בעשירות:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi, who says: Even with regard to valuations it is so: that if a wealthy person was obligated in a valuation and a poor person said: What this one said is upon me, he gives the valuation of a wealthy person. Evidently we follow the obligation of the person valuated, where he is obligated something, similar to the leper. And so a wealthy leper whose vower is poor needs no exclusion, for we derive from valuations that he brings in wealth.

notes.he: ולר' דאמר [אומר אני אף בערכין כן] דומיא דהרי שאמר קרבנו [של מצורע זה עלי] דאזלינן בתר מצורע הכי נמי אמר ר' בערכין הרי שאמר [אחד] ערכי עלי ושמע זה ואמר מה שהעריך זה [על עצמו] עלי ליתנו בשבילו אם היה נודר עשיר צריך לתת ערך עשיר אע"פ שהמדיר עני אלמא אזלינן נמי בערכין בתר השג יד דנידר לטעמא דרבי:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi, who says [I say: even with regard to valuations it is so]: similar to one who said: [The offering of this leper] is upon me, where we follow the leper, so too Rabbi says regarding valuations: if [one] said: My valuation is upon me, and another heard and said: What this one valuated [for himself] is upon me, to give it for him, then if the one vowed about was wealthy, he must give the valuation of a wealthy person, even though the one who vows for him is poor. Evidently, according to Rabbi’s reasoning, in valuations too we follow the means of the subject of the vow.

messages.text: Evidently, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: We follow the obligation of the original person valuated, even with regard to valuations. And if so, then the reasoning stated in the aforementioned baraita does not apply, and therefore a verse is not necessary to exclude a destitute person who takes a vow to provide a wealthy leper’s offering from having the leniency of bringing the offering of a destitute leper.

notes.he: הא מצורע עשיר ומדירו עני לא צריכא קרא הוא למעוטי שהרי (מעריכין) [ממתני'] למדנו דאזלינן בתר חיובא דגברא דנידר:
notes.en: But a wealthy leper whose vower is poor does not need the verse “he” to exclude, for [from the mishna] we have learned that we follow the obligation of the person who is the subject of the vow.

messages.text: Consequently, when the verse specifies: “And if he is poor,” this serves to exclude what?

notes.he: אלא הוא לרבי למעוטי מאי:
notes.en: Rather, according to Rabbi, “he” excludes what?

messages.text: The verse serves to exclude the case of a destitute leper for whom a wealthy person takes a vow.

notes.he: דמייתי בעשירות ולרבנן לא איצטריך למעוטי דהואיל דבערכין אזלינן בתר נודר במצורע נמי אזלינן בתר נודר אבל לרבי איצטריך להכי:
notes.en: To exclude a poor leper whose vower is wealthy: that he brings in wealth. And according to the Rabbis it is not necessary to exclude this, for since in valuations we follow the one who vows, with the leper too we follow the one who vows. But according to Rabbi it is necessary for this.

notes.he: דאזלינן בתר מדירו ומייתי בעשירות דהא כתיב הוא דעליה דידיה חס רחמנא ולא אמדירו:
notes.en: To exclude a poor leper whose vower is wealthy: that we follow his vower and he brings in wealth, for it is written “he”: on him the Merciful One had compassion, and not on his vower.

messages.text: In that case, it might enter your mind to say that since Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: We follow the obligation of the original person specified as the subject of the vow, therefore the wealthy person brings only the offering of the destitute leper.

notes.dh: הכא נמי בתר חיובא דגברא [אזלינן] קמ"ל
notes.he: והקשה רבינו אלחנן כיון דאמרי' נמי אליבא דרבי מצורע עני שמדירו עשיר אזלינן בתר חיובא דגברא אי לאו מיעוטא דקרא אם כן בערכין נמי נימא כן דאם אמר עני ערכי עלי ושמע עשיר ואמר מה שאמר זה עלי נותן ערך עני כיון דאין לנו מקרא למעט דלא אזלינן בתר חיובא דגברא התם ותירץ רבינו אלחנן דשאני גבי מצורע דאית לן למימר דאזלינן בתר חיובא דגברא אי לאו קרא דממעט ליה כיון שאינו נודר אלא קרבן המצורע דוקא אבל גבי ערכין דאמר העשיר מה שאמר זה העני עלי פשיטא [דלא] אזלינן בתר חיובא דגברא שהרי אם לא היה העני חייב כלום אלא שאמר העשיר ערך פלוני עלי היה נותן ערך עשיר וכל שכן אם נתחייב (קרבן) אין לנו לגרעו לעשיר ליתן ערך עני:
notes.en: Here too we follow the obligation of the person; it teaches us [otherwise]: Rabbeinu Elḥanan asked: Since we say according to Rabbi that with a poor leper whose vower is wealthy we would follow the obligation of the person were it not for the exclusion of the verse, then with valuations too let us say so: that if a poor person said: My valuation is upon me, and a wealthy person heard and said: What this one said is upon me, he gives the valuation of a poor person, since we have no verse there to exclude [it and teach] that we do not follow the obligation of the person. And Rabbeinu Elḥanan answered: The leper is different, for there we would say that we follow the obligation of the person were it not for the verse that excludes it, since he vows only the leper’s offering specifically. But with valuations, where the wealthy person said: What this poor person said is upon me, it is obvious that we do [not] follow the obligation of the person: for even if the poor person were obligated nothing, and the wealthy person said: The valuation of so-and-so is upon me, he would give the valuation of a wealthy person; all the more so when [the poor person] was obligated, we have no reason to reduce the wealthy person to giving a poor person’s valuation.

notes.dh: דסד"א הואיל ואמר רבי בתר חיובא דגברא אזלינן
notes.he: היכא דנידר בר חיובא כגון עשיר שאמר ערכי עלי דהנידר בר חיובא הוא [אזלינן בתר נידר]:
notes.en: For it might enter your mind to say: since Rabbi said we follow the obligation of the person, where the subject of the vow is obligated, for example a wealthy person who said: My valuation is upon me, where the subject of the vow is obligated, [we follow the subject of the vow].

notes.he: כיון דמצורע בר חיובא הוא ליזול בתריה והרי הוא עני ולייתי מדירו בדלות:
notes.en: Here too: since the leper is obligated, let us follow him; and he is poor, so let his vower bring in poverty.

messages.text: Consequently, the exclusion from the verse: “And if he is poor,” teaches us that in this case he brings the offering of a wealthy individual, not that of the destitute leper.

notes.he: הוא דמייתי בדלות אבל אי מדירו הוא עשיר מייתי בעשירות דכתיב כאשר תשיג יד הנודר והרי הוא משיג:
notes.en: It teaches us “he”: he brings in poverty, but if his vower is wealthy, he brings in wealth, for it is written: “According to the means of him who vowed,” and he can afford it.

messages.caption: Whose means count: in valuations the one who vows (with Rabbi’s exception), and for a leper’s offering vowed by another, as the mishna, Rabbi Yitzḥak, Rav Adda bar Ahava and the baraita work it out.

messages.text: Mishna
If when one took a vow of valuation he was destitute and he became wealthy, or if he was wealthy and became destitute, he gives the valuation in accordance with the means of a wealthy person.

notes.he: קודם נתינה או עשיר והעני קודם נתינה נותן ערך עשיר:
notes.en: Mishna. He was poor and became wealthy: before giving, or wealthy and became poor before giving, he gives the valuation of a wealthy person.

notes.he: היה עני [בשעה שהעריך ולא הספיק ליתן עד שהעשיר או עשיר והעני נותן ערך עשיר] ומפרש בגמ' האי וטעמא דר' יהודה נמי:
notes.en: He was poor [when he valuated and did not manage to give until he became wealthy, or wealthy and became poor, he gives the valuation of a wealthy person]; and it is explained in the Gemara. [A note in the printed text suggests reading: and the Gemara explains the reason of the first tanna, and the reason of Rabbi Yehuda as well.]

messages.text: This is the halakha not only in a case where one was wealthy either at the time he took the vow or at the time of payment; even if when one took a vow of valuation he was destitute and he became wealthy and again became destitute, he gives the valuation in accordance with the means of a wealthy person.
But with regard to the offerings of a leper that is not so, as the offerings that one brings are determined by his status at the time he brings them.

notes.he: שאם היה מצורע עשיר והעני או עני והעשיר הכל הולך אחר הבאת קרבנותיו כדאמר בברייתא בגמ' מצורע שהביא קרבנותיו כו' טעמא דאיקבע בקרא למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה אבל מדברי כולן נלמד דבתר הבאת קרבנותיו אזלינן:
notes.en: But with regard to offerings that is not so: for if the leper was wealthy and became poor, or poor and became wealthy, everything follows the bringing of his offerings, as is stated in the baraita in the Gemara: A leper who brought his offerings, etc. The reason is that it is fixed in the verse, for one Sage as he holds and for the other Sage as he holds; but from the words of all of them we learn that we follow the bringing of his offerings.

messages.text: Even if it is common knowledge that his father died and left him an inheritance of ten thousand dinars, or that his ship is at sea and merchandise valued at ten thousand dinars is coming into his possession, the Temple treasury has no share in it. His payment is determined solely by his present situation.

notes.he: אערכין קאי ומלתא באפי נפשיה היא. אפי' מת אביו של מעריך זה בשעה שהכהן מעריכו והניח לו ריבוא מנה או ספינתו כו'. ובגמ' מפרש לה:
notes.en: Even if his father died, etc.: this refers to valuations, and it is a matter in its own right: even if the father of this one who valuates died at the time the priest valuates him and left him ten thousand maneh, or his ship, etc. And in the Gemara it is explained. [Rashi thus reads this clause as a separate ruling about valuations, where the Davidson English joins it to the leper’s offerings.]

notes.he: אין לפרש הא בערכין אם מעריכו הכהן כשהוא עני ימתין עד שימות אביו שהיה עשיר ויתן ערך עשיר דהא אמר בתוספתא דערכין עני שהעריך עצמו אין אומרים לו יעשה מלאכה ויביא ערך עשיר אלא מוטב שיביא ערך עני ואל יביא ערך עשיר לאחר זמן אלמא משמע שאין ממתינין אלא הכי פירושו אפילו מת אביו שהיה גוסס כדמוקי לה בגמ' דקרבן מצורע אם היה אביו גוסס בשעת הבאת חטאת וקודם שהספיק להביא קרבנות מת אביו אין להקדש בהן כלום [אבל בערכין אינו כן] כיון שלא מעריכו הכהן בעניו לתת סלע ועד לא גמר לתת סלע מת אביו והעשיר נותן ערך עשיר אך קשה מאי האי דפריך בגמ' פשיטא והא הרבה אתא לאשמועינן שאם מת אביו קודם שהספיק להביא קרבנותיו והעשיר אין להקדש בהם כלום ויש לומר דקאי אמילתיה דרבי יהודה דאמר עני והעשיר וחזר והעני נותן ערך עשיר אבל בקרבנות מת אביו כגון שהיה גוסס כדמוקי ליה כגון שהיה מתחלה עשיר והעני ועתה קרוב הוא להיות עשיר מירושת אביו אפי' הכי אין להקדש בהן כלום ופריך בגמ' פשיטא דאין להקדש בהן כלום כיון שלא היה לו אותו ממון מעולם:
notes.en: But with regard to offerings [etc.], even if his father died: One cannot explain [this to mean] that with valuations, if the priest valuated him when he was poor, he waits until his father, who was wealthy, dies, and then gives the valuation of a wealthy person. For it says in the Tosefta of Arakhin: A poor person who valuated himself, we do not tell him: Do work and bring the valuation of a wealthy person; rather, it is better that he bring the valuation of a poor person than bring the valuation of a wealthy person after some time. Evidently, we do not wait. Rather, this is its explanation: even if his father died who was dying, as the Gemara [on 18a] establishes it: with the leper’s offering, if his father was dying at the time he brought the sin offering, and before he managed to bring [the rest of] his offerings his father died, the Temple has no share in them. [But with valuations it is not so]: since the priest did not valuate him as poor, to give a sela, and before he finished giving the sela his father died, and he became wealthy, he gives the valuation of a wealthy person. But it is difficult: why does the Gemara object: It is obvious? It comes to teach us a great deal: that if his father died before he managed to bring his offerings and he became wealthy, the Temple has no share in them! And one can say that it refers to the statement of Rabbi Yehuda, who said: Poor and became wealthy and again became poor, he gives the valuation of a wealthy person. But with offerings, [even if] his father died, for example, he was dying, as the Gemara establishes it, for example, he was initially wealthy and became poor, and now he is close to becoming wealthy from his father’s inheritance, even so the Temple has no share in them. And the Gemara objects: It is obvious that the Temple has no share in them, since he never had that money.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches: If he was destitute when he took the oath and he became wealthy, he gives the valuation appropriate for a wealthy individual. This is derived from the verse: “According to the means of him who vowed shall the priest valuate him” (Leviticus 27:8), and in this case he had the means of a wealthy individual when he was ready to give the donation.
messages.quote: he was destitute and he became wealthy

notes.he: משמע דבתר נתינת יד אזלינן [ולא בשעת נדר והשתא הוי עשיר]:
notes.en: “That he can afford [asher tasig yad]”: implies that we follow the time of handing over [the payment, and not the time of the vow; and now he is wealthy].

messages.text: The mishna further teaches that one who was wealthy and became destitute also gives the valuation as though he was wealthy. This is derived from the beginning of the same verse: “According to [al pi] the means of him who vowed shall the priest valuate him.” The phrase al pi serves to emphasize the moment when the person uttered the vow with his mouth [peh], and at that moment he was wealthy.
messages.quote: he was wealthy and became destitute

notes.dh: גמ' עשיר והעני אשר תשיג יד הנודר
notes.he: דמשמע בתר שעת נדר אזלינן:
notes.en: Gemara. Wealthy and became poor: “According to the means of him who vowed”: which implies that we follow the time of the vow.

notes.dh: על פי אשר תשיג יד הנודר
notes.he: משמע בתר פה אזלינן היינו כשעת הנדר:
notes.en: “According to [al pi] the means of him who vowed”: implies that we follow the mouth [peh], that is, the time of the vow.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Yehuda says: Even if one made a valuation when he was destitute and he became wealthy and again became destitute, he gives the valuation according to the means of a wealthy person.
messages.quote: he was destitute and he became wealthy and again became destitute

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda? The verse states: “But if he is too poor for your valuation” (Leviticus 27:8). The word order serves to emphasize “he,” which indicates that he is considered poor only if he remains in his state of poverty from his beginning until his end of involvement with the vow.

notes.he: עד שיהא במכותו [מתחלתו ועד סופו] אבל אם העשיר בינתים נותן ערך עשיר:
notes.en: Until he is in his poverty [from his beginning until his end]: but if he became wealthy in between, he gives the valuation of a wealthy person.

messages.text: If that is so, then when the verse similarly states with regard to a destitute leper: “And if he is poor” (Leviticus 14:21), so too, Rabbi Yehuda should maintain that he is considered poor only if he is in his state of poverty from his beginning until his end of bringing the leper’s offering, but if he was wealthy in between he should be obligated to bring the offering of a wealthy individual, even if he is now poor.

notes.he: ואם דל הוא דכתיב במצורע:
notes.en: “And if he is poor”: which is written with regard to a leper.

messages.text: And if you would say that indeed, this is the halakha, but didn’t we learn in a mishna (Nega’im 14:11):

With regard to a leper who brought his offerings when he was destitute, and subsequently became wealthy, or he brought his offerings when he was wealthy and then became destitute, everything follows the sin offering that the leper brings. If he was wealthy when he brought the sin offering he brings the burnt offering of a wealthy individual; if he was destitute when he brought the sin offering he brings the burnt offering of a destitute individual. This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

notes.he: קצת קרבנותיו:
notes.en: Who brought his offerings: some of his offerings.

notes.he: אם הביא חטאת בהמה בעשירות מביא נמי עולת בהמה ואם הביא חטאת העוף בעניות אע"פ שהעשיר מביא נמי עולה בעניות:
notes.en: Everything follows the sin offering: if he brought an animal sin offering in wealth, he also brings an animal burnt offering; and if he brought a bird sin offering in poverty, even though he became wealthy he also brings a burnt offering in poverty.

notes.he: אחד מקרבנותיו כשהוא עני והעשיר קודם שהביא האחרים:
notes.en: Who brought his offerings: one of his offerings when he was poor, and he became wealthy before he brought the others.

notes.he: [או הביא אחד כשהוא עשיר והעני הכל הולך אחר חטאת שאם הביא חטאת העוף בדלות אע"ג דהעשיר מייתי נמי עולת (חטאת) העוף בדלות או אם הביא חטאת בהמה בעשירות אע"ג דהעני יביא עולת בהמה:
notes.en: Or he brought one when he was wealthy and became poor: everything follows the sin offering: for if he brought a bird sin offering in poverty, even though he became wealthy he also brings a bird burnt offering in poverty; or if he brought an animal sin offering in wealth, even though he became poor he brings an animal burnt offering.

messages.text: Everything, i.e., the sin offering and the burnt offering, follows his status at the time the leper’s guilt offering is brought.

notes.he: שאם הביא אשמו בעשירות אע"ג דהעני יביא הכל בעשירות. ואם הביא אשם כשהוא עני אע"ג דהעשיר הואיל ובעניותו התחיל להביא אשם יביא השאר בדלות:
notes.en: Everything follows the guilt offering: for if he brought his guilt offering in wealth, even though he became poor he brings everything in wealth; and if he brought the guilt offering when he was poor, even though he became wealthy, since he began to bring the guilt offering in his poverty, he brings the rest in poverty.

messages.text: Everything follows the offering of the birds, which are brought by the leper seven days earlier as part of his purification process.

notes.he: שתי צפורין חיות שהוא מביא לצורך הזאה קודם תגלחת אם בשעה שהזו עליו הוי עני מביא בעניות קרבנותיו ואם באותה שעה היה עשיר מביא כל קרבנותיו בעשירות:
notes.en: After the birds: the two live birds that he brings for the sprinkling before the shaving. If at the time they sprinkled on him he was poor, he brings his offerings in poverty; and if at that time he was wealthy, he brings all his offerings in wealth.

messages.text: Clearly, everyone agrees that one brings the offerings of the destitute even if he is not destitute from the beginning until the end of the process.

notes.he: וכן נמי הכל הולך אחר שתי צפרים אם הביאן בעניותו אע"ג דשוב העשיר יביא השאר בדלות אלמא דלא אמרינן עד שיהא בדלותו מתחלתו ועד סופו:
notes.en: And likewise, everything follows the two birds: if he brought them in his poverty, even though he afterward became wealthy, he brings the rest in poverty. Evidently we do not say: until he is in his poverty from his beginning until his end.

messages.text: And all three of these tanna’im derived their opinions from one verse, which deals with the destitute leper: “This is the law of him in whom is the mark of leprosy, whose means do not suffice for that which pertains to his purification” (Leviticus 14:32).
messages.lead: The Gemara explains: It was stated with regard to this dispute that Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:

verse.he: זֹאת תּוֹרַת אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ נֶגַע צָרָעַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא־תַשִּׂיג יָדוֹ בְּטׇהֳרָתוֹ׃ {פ}
verse.en: Such is the ritual for one who has a scaly affection and whose means for purification are limited.

notes.he: דגזירת הכתוב היא:
notes.en: They derived from one verse: for it is a Torah edict.

notes.he: דמשום הכי פליגי בהא דמקרא אחד דרשו כו']:
notes.en: Wasn’t it stated about this: that this is why they disagree in this, that they derived from one verse, etc.

messages.text: Rabbi Shimon holds: The individual’s status depends on an item that atones, and what is it? The sin offering.

notes.he: דהכי כתיב במצורע עני (ויקרא י״ד:ל״ב) וכפר עליו הכהן וסמיך ליה האי קרא דזאת תורת אשר בו נגע צרעת וגו' דמשמע אשר לא תשיג ידו בשעת כפרה יהא לו תורה זו של דלות ואף על פי שהשיגה ידו אחר כך:
notes.en: An item that atones: for so it is written with regard to the poor leper: “And the priest shall atone for him” [Leviticus 14:31], and adjacent to it is this verse: “This is the law of him in whom is the mark of leprosy,” etc., which implies: one whose means do not suffice at the time of atonement shall have this law of poverty, even though his means suffice afterward.

notes.he: על חטא והיינו חטאת דאמרינן לעיל בעון (ח') [שבעה] דברים נגעים באין וחטאת מכפרת היינו טהרתו והכל הולך אחריו:
notes.en: An item that atones: for sin, that is, the sin offering. For we said above: Leprous marks come on account of seven things, and the sin offering atones; that is his purification, and everything follows it.

messages.text: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: His status depends on an item that renders him fit to enter the Temple and eat consecrated food, and what is it? The guilt offering.

notes.he: דהכי משמע אשר לא תשיג ידו בשעת טהרה תהא לו תורת עניות וטהרה זהו אשם המכשירו לבא במקדש ולאכול בקדשים שמדם האשם הוא נותן על בהונות ותנוך אזנים:
notes.en: An item that renders fit: for so it implies: one whose means do not suffice at the time of his purification shall have the law of poverty. And the purification is the guilt offering, which renders him fit to enter the Temple and to eat consecrated food, for he places from the blood of the guilt offering on the thumbs and on the ridge of the ears.

notes.dh: רבי יהודה סבר דבר המכשירו ומאי ניהו אשם
notes.he: וא"ת האמר לקמן פר' האומר משקלי עלי (ערכין דף כא.) (ובפרק שלישי דנזיר) (דף יט) כשם שחטאתו ואשמו מעכבת כך עולתו מעכבת חטאת ועולה הא לא מכשיר כי אם אשם וי"ל דהא ודאי כולהו מעכבי לאכול בקדשים דהא בחטאת שייכא ביה כפרה יותר מאשם שהרי אשם אין כל עיקרו אלא להכשיר את המצורע שהוא מזין עליו [ועל] הבהונות מדם האשם לכך קרי ליה דבר המכשירו:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda holds: the item that renders him fit, and what is it? The guilt offering: And if you say: But it says below in the chapter HaOmer Mishkali Alai (Arakhin 21a) (and in the third chapter of Nazir, 19a): Just as his sin offering and his guilt offering are indispensable, so his burnt offering is indispensable. [So] the sin offering and the burnt offering [are also indispensable], yet only the guilt offering is called what renders fit? And one can say: Certainly all of them are indispensable for eating consecrated food; for the sin offering, atonement applies to it more than to the guilt offering, since the guilt offering’s whole essence is only to render the leper fit, for he places [blood] from the guilt offering on him, [on] the thumbs. Therefore he calls it the item that renders him fit.

notes.he: בקדשים ולחזור לאכלו היינו אשם:
notes.en: An item that renders him fit: for consecrated food, to return to eating it; that is, the guilt offering.

messages.text: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov holds: His status depends on that which causes him ritual purity, and what is it? The sacrificial birds, as the rite of the birds partially purifies him and enables him to bring the rest of his offerings and to complete his purification process.

notes.he: צפרין גורמין לו טהרה שכל זמן שאינו מביא צפרין אינו יכול לגלח:
notes.en: The birds cause him purity: for as long as he does not bring the birds, he cannot shave.

notes.dh: הגורם לו טהרה ומאי ניהו צפרין
notes.he: דכתיב ולקח למיטהר וגו':
notes.en: That which causes him purity, and what is it? The birds: as it is written: “Then shall the priest command to take for him that is to be purified [two living clean birds]” (Leviticus 14:4).

messages.text: If so, in the particular case of a leper bringing his own offerings, it is a Torah edict that one does not need to be destitute throughout the entire process, which is why, with regard to one who takes a vow to bring the offerings of a leper, Rabbi Yehuda does not derive from the verse: “And if he is poor,” that he is considered poor only if he is in a state of poverty from the beginning, i.e., when he takes the vow, until the end, i.e., when he fulfills it.

messages.caption: When a leper’s means change while he brings his offerings, three Tanna’im name the offering that fixes his status, and Rav’s explanation of how each reads the same verse.

messages.text: But in that case why do I need the exclusion in the verse: “And if he is poor”?

notes.he: ואלא הואיל דלא דרשינן [אם דל הוא] עד שיהא בדלות מתחלתו ועד סופו:
notes.en: But since we do not expound [“if he is poor”] to mean: until he is in poverty from his beginning until his end,

notes.he: דאם דל הוא במצורע למה לי:
notes.en: [Rather,] “he”: why do I need “if he is poor” with regard to a leper?

messages.text: According to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, it is necessary in accordance with his opinion stated earlier, that it serves to exclude a wealthy individual who vows to provide the offering of a destitute leper, i.e., he must bring the offering of a wealthy individual. And according to the Rabbis, it is necessary in accordance with their opinion, that it serves to exclude a destitute individual who vows to provide the offering of the wealthy leper, and he must bring the offering of a wealthy individual.

notes.he: כדדרשינן לעיל:
notes.en: According to Rabbi as he holds, etc.: as we expounded above.

notes.he: כדאמרינן לעיל לרבי למעוטי מצורע עני ומדירו עשיר ולרבנן למעוטי מצורע עשיר ומדירו עני:
notes.en: According to Rabbi as he holds: as we said above: according to Rabbi, to exclude a poor leper whose vower is wealthy, and according to the Rabbis, to exclude a wealthy leper whose vower is poor.

messages.text: If that is so, that Rabbi Yehuda maintains that the phrase: “And if he is poor,” teaches that one is classified as destitute only if he is destitute from beginning to end, he should similarly derive from a verse that deals with testimony: “And he is a witness, whether he has seen or known, if he does not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity” (Leviticus 5:1), that this applies only if the witness is fit to testify from his beginning, when he obtained the information about which he is testifying, until his end, when he testifies.

verse.he: וְנֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תֶחֱטָא וְשָׁמְעָה קוֹל אָלָה וְהוּא עֵד אוֹ רָאָה אוֹ יָדָע אִם־לוֹא יַגִּיד וְנָשָׂא עֲוֺנוֹ׃
verse.en:
If a person incurs guilt—
When someone has heard a public imprecation but (although able to testify as having seen or learned of the matter) has not given information and thus is subject to punishment;

notes.he: אלא מעתה לרבי יהודה דדריש ואם מך הוא עד שיהא במכותו כו' הכי נמי כו':
notes.en: But if so, according to Rabbi Yehuda, who expounds “but if he is too poor”: until he is in his poverty, etc., so too, etc.

notes.he: [והוא עד עד שיהא כשר:
notes.en: “And he is a witness”: until he is fit.

messages.text: And if you would say that indeed, that is the halakha with regard to the qualification of a witness, but isn’t it taught in a baraita:

If someone knew testimony about another before he, the one who knew the testimony, became the other’s son-in-law, and then he became his son-in-law; or when he was able to hear, and then he became a deaf-mute; or when he could see, and he subsequently became blind; or while he was halakhically competent, and he then became an imbecile; in all these cases, he is disqualified from testifying.

notes.he: סומא פסול לעדות דבעינן או ראה:
notes.en: A blind person is unfit for testimony: for we require “or he has seen.”

notes.he: בן דעת:
notes.en: Competent [shafui]: of sound mind.

messages.text: But if someone knew testimony about another before he became his son-in-law, and he then became his son-in-law,

notes.dh: עד שלא נעשה חתנו ונעשה חתנו (ונעשה חתנו) ואח"כ מתה בתו כשר
notes.he: מיירי בשאין בנים לבתו כיון דמוקמי' ליה הכא כר"י דאית ליה לר"י (סנהדרין כז:) היה חתנו ומתה בתו אם יש לה בנים הימנו הרי זה קרוב אבל אם אין לו בנים אין זה קרוב:
notes.en: Before he became his son-in-law, and he became his son-in-law, and afterward his daughter died, he is fit: this speaks where his daughter has no children, since we establish it here in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who holds (Sanhedrin 27b): If he was his son-in-law and his daughter died, if she has children from him, he is a relative; but if he has no children, he is not a relative.

messages.text: Continues on 18a: the baraita goes on that if afterward his wife died, or the deaf-mute, the blind or the imbecile recovered, he is fit, for anyone whose beginning and end are in a state of fitness is fit; so testimony too is not required to be fit from beginning to end.
